methodological_rigor.justification: The authors use CRISPR/Cas9 knock-in of ERCC6-M1097V in several PCa cell lines including PCa2 (AA-derived) and measure UV/CDDP survival, CPD kinetics by dot blot, and DNA-dependent ATPase on IP-purified tagged protein. Controls (siRNA knockdown, NT1-Nek1-KO) are reasonable, but experiments are limited to one or two clones per cell line with no replicate biological lines, no blinded scoring, and no PDX or in vivo validation (authors acknowledge this). Statistical analysis is limited to Student's t-tests on linear regression slopes from Incucyte with no multiplicity correction, no formal sample-size justification, and effect sizes are not systematically reported; standard errors are used without confidence intervals.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a preclinical cell-line mechanistic study (LoE 5 per Oxford CEBM preclinical mapping) with no patient data, clinical endpoints, or in vivo tumor models. While the authors frame findings in the context of AA prostate cancer disparities in Louisiana and propose synthetic lethality with CDDP+J54, translational relevance remains speculative: no xenograft, no PDX, no biomarker validation in patient tissue is presented. The clinical argument rests on a single prior germline-frequency report and unpublished observations.

reporting_quality.justification: No recognized reporting checklist (ARRIVE is most applicable for preclinical though this is cell-line only) is explicitly addressed. Methods omit key details: numbers of biological/technical replicates per condition, clone numbers beyond a representative, UV dose in mJ/cm2 for the proliferation experiments (only time exposures given), randomization/blinding during CPD quantification, and quantitative image analysis pipelines. There is no data or code availability statement, no repository links, and several text passages (Methods, Results) are duplicated verbatim, suggesting incomplete editorial polish.

novelty_literature.justification: First functional characterization of the ERCC6-M1097V variant introduced by CRISPR knock-in at the endogenous locus in PCa cell lines is a meaningful, targeted extension of prior epidemiological observations (Yadav et al. 2020). The counterintuitive finding that M1097V confers greater UV tolerance and faster CPD removal is novel within PCa but incremental in the broader ERCC6/CSB literature, where variant function has been studied in other cancers. No new mechanism, structural rationale, or pathway is established.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is readable but disorganized: Results and Discussion contain large duplicated paragraphs (the M1097V UV-resistance description appears twice), figure legends are terse (e.g., Figure 3 lacks units, n, and statistical test per panel), and Figure 6 uses 'CPT' in the legend while the body describes cisplatin (CDDP), creating ambiguity. The abstract frames speculative therapeutic proposals as if demonstrated, and multiple sentences reference 'unpublished' results that drive key conclusions.

key_strengths: Genomic knock-in of M1097V at the endogenous ERCC6 locus with heterozygous and homozygous clones is a technically appropriate approach to an underexplored variant
Inclusion of the AA-derived PCa2 line and siRNA knockdown controls strengthens the causal link between ERCC6 function and CPD clearance
Addresses a documented health-disparities question (AA prostate cancer in Louisiana) that is clinically important
key_concerns: Statistical analysis limited to t-tests on regression slopes with no multiplicity correction, no confidence intervals, and unclear replication structure
Conclusions rest on a small number of clones per cell line with no orthogonal validation (e.g., PDX, in vivo, or independent biological replicates of clones)
ATPase comparison uses an overexpression construct that the authors themselves note is confounded by the ERCC6-PGBD3 fusion, weakening the biochemical claim
Manuscript contains substantial duplicated text between Results and Discussion and inconsistent abbreviation use (CPT vs CDDP in Figure 6)
No data/code availability statement; reporting-standard adherence (ARRIVE-like elements for preclinical work) is minimal
Therapeutic proposals (CDDP+J54 synthetic lethality) are advanced without any experimental test in this work
chief_reviewer.rationale: A preclinical, mechanistic cell-line study with a narrowly scoped and incompletely supported claim, limited statistical rigor, and presentation issues; appropriate for a lower-tier specialty journal after major revision.
